messages:
oliver: heads-up — ACME flagged a subtle regression after the rollout last night. They say tiny template changes (even a trailing period) now produce completely different outputs. they pasted an example and said it broke a production alert. :warning:

ACME (quoted): "Previously: 'Summarize in 2 bullets: <doc>' -> good, concise bullets. After rollout, changing to 'Summarize in 2 bullets: <doc>.' (note trailing period) returns a list of unrelated QA items."

oliver: minimal reproducer they gave (sanitized):
```bash
curl -s -X POST "https://api.redwood.inference/v1/completions" \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" \n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n  -d '{"model":"redwood-v1.1","input":"Summarize in 2 bullets: Today we launched..."}'
```

-- expected: two concise bullets summarizing launch.
-- observed (with trailing period in prompt): unrelated list of tasks.

karla: yikes. customer is mid-tier PLG -> sales notified, they flagged as high impact. ACME says this broke an automated email summary job. can you triage, @samir ? :eyes:

support-bot: Incident created #INC-2026-298 (severity: P2) — assigned to support oncall.

samir: onto it. can you attach the raw request/response headers and the model variant? we need model tag + rollout id + exact prompt. also any tokenization evidence would help.

oliver: attaching what ACME pasted (sanitized). they used model id 'redwood-v1.1' in the UI. no explicit model_patch id shown. response snippets:

```
// request.input: "Summarize in 2 bullets: <doc>."
// response.text: "- setup monitoring
- add onboarding tasks"  // totally wrong
```

jordan: FYI rollout logs show a serving change at 2026-03-14T23:15Z — deploy-bot logged model variant redwood-v1.1-quant-small promoted from canary to 100% (rollout id rdo-3345).

deploy-bot: rollout rdo-3345: redwood-v1.1-quant-small — started 2026-03-14T23:15Z, canary->100% by 2026-03-14T23:40Z.

maya: can we reproduce locally with that quantized variant? if yes, we'll confirm if it's a quantization/tokenizer effect or model weight change.

samir: trying repro now with the exact variant and tokenizer commit used in rdo-3345. can you paste the exact prompt text (including trailing spaces/punctuation)? tiny differences matter.

oliver: pasted exact user prompt in a private link (sensitive) and also included two failing examples: one with trailing period, one without. both are in the incident attachment.

samir: quick update — I can reproduce the divergence on redwood-v1.1-quant-small with the same prompt. no runtime errors, purely semantic change. when I swap to redwood-v1.1-quant-large (previous variant) the output matches expected.

jordan: that suggests the quant profile or tokenizer normalization changed in the small variant. checking kernel selection notes — there was a tokenizer normalization tweak in tokenizer v2.2 that got bundled with the small quant build to reduce OOMs.

samir: digging into logits/attention patterns. preliminary: tokenization split differs for punctuation in a few anchors, causing downstream decoding to favor different spans. small quantization amplified the effect.

karla: action items for communication: 1) give ACME a mitigation (pin model or rollback), 2) timeline for root cause + fix, 3) ETA for preventive test. I'll draft comms once we have mitigation.

maya: mitigation options: a) route ACME's tenant to redwood-v1.1-quant-large until fix, b) roll back rdo-3345 to previous variant globally, c) add a per-tenant routing rule (fastest). Recommend (a) for minimal blast radius.

oliver: ACME asks for a quick fix; they'd prefer pinning to previous behavior. can we do tenant-level pinning now?

jordan: yes, runtime supports per-tenant routing. I'll create a temporary route rule: tenant:acme -> redwood-v1.1-quant-large. will apply after change approval.

deploy-bot: route change request created: route-req-887. awaiting approval from eng-runtime + cs.

samir: long term fix — we'll add a regression test in the prompt-template suite that fuzzes tiny punctuation variants across quant profiles. also need to test tokenizer normalization diffs.

oliver: repro steps I ran (for triage):
```bash
# reproducible script (sanitized)
python repro.py --model redwood-v1.1-quant-small --prompt "Summarize in 2 bullets: Example doc."
python repro.py --model redwood-v1.1-quant-large --prompt "Summarize in 2 bullets: Example doc."
# compare outputs, diff shows mismatch introduced by -quant-small
```

samir: confirmed. I'll open ENG-ML ticket with logs + weight diffs and assign to myself. if tokenizer v2.2 is the culprit we can unbundle it from the small variant and re-run quantization.

karla: ACME update plan: propose tenant pin for 24-72h, apology, and promise of regression test + ETA for fix. can someone draft the support note? I can review and send.

oliver: drafting now. will include mitigation steps and ask them to confirm non-production tests.

jordan: applying tenant route after approval now — ETA ~10m. will post when done. :white_check_mark:

deploy-bot: route route-req-887: applied -> tenant:acme pinned to redwood-v1.1-quant-large.

samir: next steps (internal): 1) isolate tokenizer/quant interaction, 2) reproduce minimal tokenization delta, 3) re-quantize variant without tokenizer change OR revert tokenizer change in small build, 4) add fuzz tests to prompt-template CI.

karla: tagging owners: @samir (eng-ml) lead, @jordan (eng-runtime) apply mitigation, @oliver support comms. I'll schedule a quick sync in 30m with ACME if necessary. :phone:

oliver: thanks team. I'll keep this thread updated with customer replies.

support-bot: Incident #INC-2026-298 updated: owner=samir, status=investigating.
